chembl.note: CHEMBL5875133 independently verified live via get_drug_info -- it is a REAL ChEMBL molecule record (molecular_weight=440.45, no pref_name, mechanism_of_action='Not available'), so this is NOT a fabricated identifier (gate passes) but IS an incorrect/misleading match: the tool's fuzzy fallback (ChEMBL's relevance-ranked search.json endpoint) returned a real molecule as its 'top hit' for a fully fabricated compound name, and resolve_compound_name has no confidence/similarity threshold to suppress a low-quality fuzzy hit and fall back to no_match. Compare CHEMBL-ZERO-01, a different fabricated name, which DID correctly return no_match -- the fuzzy path's behavior on nonsense input is inconsistent/query-dependent.

per_case_results.first_time_measured: resolve_compound_name's fuzzy-fallback path on genuinely nonexistent compound names was never exercised on any dev/validation case (all 21 dev/validation ChEMBL cases had a real gold entity); this is the first empirical measurement of that path's failure mode

pubmed.query_concept_coverage_note: trivially 1.0 for all cases -- the frozen architecture sends the raw user query directly to retrieve() with no query-compilation/rewriting step, so there is no opportunity for concept loss between ResearchQuery and the retrieval call

P50/P90/P95 at n=6 are not statistically meaningful point estimates -- reported as observed order statistics only, per the gate plan's instruction not to conflate latency components; this run did not separately instrument BM25/FAISS/reranker sub-stage latency (only end-to-end retrieve() time was captured, since the frozen retrieve() call is a single opaque call per the frozen config -- sub-stage timing was not available without modifying retrieval/retriever.py, which is out of scope).

chembl.zero_result_correctness_note: 1/2 zero-result-expected cases correct: CHEMBL-ZERO-01 ('ZZZNOTADRUGNAME123') correctly returned no_match; NEG-ABSENT-01's chembl leg ('Zorblatinix-9X') incorrectly returned match_type='fuzzy' with a real, non-null chembl_id (CHEMBL5875133). This inconsistency (one fabricated name -> no_match, a different fabricated name -> a confident-looking fuzzy hit) had NEVER been measured before this run: chembl_zero_result is a 1-count category in the whole 61-case benchmark and it landed in development... actually it is the ONLY zero-result chembl case and it is in phase4_heldout; NEG-ABSENT-01's chembl leg is likewise phase4_heldout-only. So resolve_compound_name's behavior on fabricated/absent names is being measured here for the first time in this project.

fabricated_source_identifiers.evidence: every PMID, ChEMBL ID, and (absent) NCT ID returned across all 12 cases was independently verifiable as a real record from its respective public API/corpus; CHEMBL5875133 (the NEG-ABSENT-01 fuzzy-match concern) was live-verified via get_drug_info and is a real ChEMBL molecule, not a fabrication -- it is a WRONG_ENTITY/precision defect, not an ID-fabrication gate violation

source_id_corruption.evidence: all PMIDs are well-formed numeric strings, all returned ChEMBL IDs match ^CHEMBL\d+$, no malformed/truncated/mangled identifiers observed in any of the 12 raw results

cross_source_id_collision.evidence: PMIDs, ChEMBL IDs, and NCT IDs use disjoint, unambiguous formats; no identifier from one source's result set could be mistaken for another source's identifier format in any of the 12 cases

secrets_or_auth_headers_in_retrieval_tra.evidence: grepped the full raw result trace (/tmp/heldout_raw_results.json) for key/token/secret patterns -- zero matches; PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov/ChEMBL are all unauthenticated public APIs for the calls made in this run (no API key was used or could have leaked), confirmed by reading config/settings.py's secret-field definitions (only NVIDIA_API_KEY and CEREBRAS_API_KEY exist as SecretStr fields in this project, neither is used by any of the three retrieval tools measured here)

consistent_findings: PubMed RAG positive-case recall/MRR (1.0/1.0/1.0 recall@1/5/10, MRR 1.0 on n=4) is consistent with (not contradicted by; in fact stronger than) the dev/validation-measured 0.773 Recall@10 / 0.636 MRR reported in phase4_frozen_config.json -- small held-out n and an easier narrow-constraint-heavy case mix plausibly explain the higher point estimate; no regression observed.

ChEMBL positive-case resolution (aspirin->CHEMBL25, exact_preferred_name, rank 1) is consistent with the dev/validation resolve_compound_name methodology's measured Recall@10=1.0, MRR=0.898 (phase4_chembl_resolution_results.json).

ClinicalTrials zero-result handling (2/2 correct empty returns) is consistent with the AREA[Phase]/query.term fix already documented as FIXED in phase4_failure_analysis.json -- no new ClinicalTrials defect observed.
No hard safety gate violation occurred, consistent with phase4_failure_analysis.json's hard_gate_violations_found: 0 on dev/validation.

new_findings_not_previously_documented.finding: PubMed RAG architecture has no zero-result / relevance-threshold mechanism: for a fabricated-drug-name query, retrieve() always returns k=10 nearest-neighbor chunks regardless of true relevance (observed cross-encoder scores strongly negative, -4.1 to -8.7, yet all 10 were still returned as if they were candidate results).
new_findings_not_previously_documented.why_new: pubmed_zero_result is a 1-count category across the entire 61-case benchmark and that single case (PM-ZERO-01) was assigned to phase4_heldout -- this exact behavior was never exercised in development or validation measurement, so this is the first empirical evidence of it.
new_findings_not_previously_documented.gate_impact: none -- no fabricated ID was produced, so no hard gate is violated
new_findings_not_previously_documented.correctness_impact: real: a downstream consumer that does not itself apply a relevance/score threshold to retrieve()'s output could present 10 irrelevant PMIDs as if they were supporting citations for a nonexistent drug. This is an architectural property of the frozen, already-selected top-k similarity retriever, not a bug introduced by this measurement, and it was implicitly foreseeable from the architecture description (no existence-check layer exists anywhere in the frozen config) -- but it had not actually been measured before now.
new_findings_not_previously_documented.severity_assessment: moderate, pre-existing/architectural, not a regression -- does not on its own indicate a NEW defect introduced since the freeze, but is new EVIDENCE that a previously-untested edge case behaves in a way worth the orchestrating session's attention before relying on PubMed RAG results as self-certifying relevance.

new_findings_not_previously_documented.finding: ChEMBL resolve_compound_name's fuzzy-fallback path is inconsistent on fabricated/nonexistent compound names: 'ZZZNOTADRUGNAME123' correctly returns match_type='no_match', but 'Zorblatinix-9X' returns match_type='fuzzy' with a real, non-null chembl_id (CHEMBL5875133, independently verified as a real but unrelated ChEMBL molecule with no preferred name). The fuzzy path has no confidence/similarity threshold and simply takes ChEMBL's own ElasticSearch top hit whenever that endpoint returns anything at all for the input string.
new_findings_not_previously_documented.why_new: all 21 dev/validation ChEMBL cases had a real gold entity to resolve (chembl_zero_result, the only fabricated-name test category, is a 1-count category and it too landed in phase4_heldout) -- this fuzzy-fallback failure mode on genuinely nonexistent input was never exercised before this run.
new_findings_not_previously_documented.gate_impact: none -- CHEMBL5875133 is a real record, not a fabricated identifier, so the fabricated-source-identifiers gate is not violated
new_findings_not_previously_documented.correctness_impact: real: a caller that treats any non-null chembl_id as a usable answer (rather than checking match_type=='fuzzy' and treating it with appropriate skepticism) would present a real but entirely unrelated drug record as if it were information about a nonexistent compound named 'Zorblatinix-9X'. This directly undermines the intended NO_RESULTS/abstention behavior the NEG-ABSENT-01 case is designed to test.
new_findings_not_previously_documented.severity_assessment: moderate, newly discovered, affects the specific and narrow 'fabricated compound name' input class -- 1 of the 3 ChEMBL held-out cases (33%), though only 2 total zero-result-type ChEMBL cases exist in the entire benchmark so this is a very small n to generalize a rate from. Worth flagging clearly to the orchestrating session as new evidence; not confirmed here as a widespread problem across the whole ChEMBL surface (the 21 dev/validation positive-entity cases and 1 correct no_match case show no analogous issue).

already_accepted_limitations_reflected_h: ChEMBL search_by_target first-hit WRONG_ENTITY heuristic (accepted limitation per phase4_failure_analysis.json) was NOT exercised in phase4_heldout at all -- no heldout case calls search_by_target, so this accepted limitation could not recur or be contradicted here.
ClinicalTrials MS-06-style single ranking miss (accepted limitation) was not exercised either -- no positive-gold multi-result ClinicalTrials case exists in phase4_heldout.

scope_caveats: This measurement calls retrieve()/search_trials()/resolve_compound_name() directly, matching the frozen architecture's retrieval functions exactly as specified. It does NOT invoke agent/orchestration/ code, per the task's explicit prohibition on modifying or (by extension) exercising those layers as the decision-making abstention/routing logic. The 3 abstention-expected cases (NEG-UNSUPPORTED-01/02, NEG-ABSTAIN-AMBIG-01) are therefore reported as 'no tool call made, consistent with no supporting operation existing' rather than as a full end-to-end confirmation that the live agent correctly abstains.

ClinicalTrials call arguments (condition/intervention/status/phase) were hand-compiled from each case's query/gold fields by this measurement harness, standing in for the orchestration layer's real query-compilation step (which is out of scope here) -- this matches how the case's own gold verification was done (a human-constructed live API call), not a test of the orchestration layer's own compilation correctness.

PubMed sub-stage latency (BM25 vs FAISS vs cross-encoder rerank) was not separately instrumented -- only end-to-end retrieve() latency was captured, since instrumenting internals would require modifying retrieval/retriever.py, which is out of scope for this pure-measurement task.
